## How they got there
Arsenal secured their place as the 2025-26 runner-up by navigating a field of 24 knockout teams, ultimately falling to Paris Saint-Germain in the final via penalties (1-1, 3-4). Their path was defined by elite efficiency; they recorded a goal difference per game of 2.38 and points per game of 3.0. Both metrics placed them at the 100th percentile compared to that season's teams and ranked in the 97th and 99th percentiles respectively against all Champions League teams since 2011-12. Defensively, they were equally formidable, limiting opponent shots on target per game to just 2.8, a figure that sits at the 3rd percentile for the season and the 8th overall.

## Would the model have picked them?
Despite never seeing this specific season, the predictive model would almost certainly have selected Arsenal as a top contender. The model assigned a 25.6% probability of reaching the final, which is significantly higher than the base rate of 8.3%. This high confidence placed them at rank 2 among all knockout teams based on that probability alone. Their expected knockout stage was calculated at 1.52, suggesting the model anticipated they would reach deep into the tournament. The primary driver for this positive outlook was their goal difference per game, which contributed +0.83 to the model's expectation of advancing further than a quarter-finalist.

## Weak spots
While dominant in attack and defense, Arsenal showed statistical vulnerabilities that pulled the model's prediction down. Their passing volume was a notable weakness; with 450 passes per game, they ranked only at the 39th percentile for the season and 34th historically, contributing -0.17 to their expected stage. Similarly, their high output of 50.1 attacks per game (81st percentile) was viewed negatively by the model, resulting in a -0.14 contribution. The team also covered 118.5 km per game, ranking at the 75th percentile for the season and 82nd historically, which further dragged down their projected performance by another -0.14.
